newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Tomkins cash marked for new buys.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Tomkins cash marked for new buys.

text.p: UK engineering-to-baking combine Tomkins Plc said on Monday it was not likely to return its cash pile to shareholders, citing opportunities for a number of possible acquisitions this year which offered better value.
The comments by Gregory Hutchings, executive chairman, in an interview with Reuters, refutes rumours of a possible return of the 366.8 million stg in cash to shareholders.
Speculation about this helped push the shares up in recent weeks. Hutchings said "We see sufficient (acquisition) opportununities to hold on to our cash for the time being."
Hutchings said the group was likely to make a number of smaller buys. "It won't be one major deal, but it could be worth up to 200 million pounds," he said.
If the opportunities failed to be realised Tomkins could then consider the best way of returning value to shareholders, including the buyback option, he added.
The comments came after Tomkins announced a better than expected set of half year results, with profits up 34 percent to 168.8 million stg, above the average analyst forecast of 160 million.
The interim payout was 3.06 pence per share, versus 2.7.
The group is looking to sell off some of its small non-manufacturing units and is already in talks with some buyers, it said. But the chairman refused to comment further.

He said he was very pleased with the performance of the group in the six months to November 2 1996. Earnings growth was ahead of the sector, he said. "Organic growth, if you strip out the Gates acquisition and the effect of the dollar, was near to 10 percent.."
Hutchings said the share price should continue to outperform on the back of its results. Tomkins shares are currently trading up eight pence at 277 1/2.
The Gates company, acquired for $1.1 billion last year, performed "very much as expected," with margins up and cash generation of 52 million stg.
The group plans to invest in expanding Gates presence in India, China and Latin America in particular.
Stg's rise against the dollar and mark has not had a notable impact on the company, said the chairman.
On the dollar/stg cross, he said the group was locked at $1.52 to the stg for the rest of the year. The amount of mark-denominated business was minimal, he said.

On market conditions, the U.S. is seen remaining firm, with the UK described as mixed. The French market is expected to continue to suffer due to the economic problems "but the amount of (French) sales is very small within the group."
